A soybean-style inbred line breeding pipeline

Source: R/line-pipeline.R
line_pipeline.Rd

A ready-made alphasim_program() for the pipeline most public soybean (and other self-pollinated crop) programs run: cross elite parents, advance the progeny to inbred lines by single-seed descent, test every line in a preliminary yield trial (PYT), advance the best to an advanced yield trial (AYT), release the best AYT lines and recycle the best as parents for the next cycle. Any argument can be tuned with tune().

Usage

line_pipeline(..., founders = asr_founders())

Arguments

...

Arguments to set or tune: n_parents, n_crosses, progeny_per_cross, line_generation, generations_per_year, pyt_locations, pyt_reps, n_ayt, ayt_locations, ayt_reps, n_release, cycles, gxe_var, cross_cost, ssd_cost, plot_cost, pyt_plot_cost, pyt_error, offseason_cost, max_plots, max_cost, and any asr_founders() field such as plot_h2.

founders

An asr_founders() recipe.

Value

A line_pipeline spec.

How one cycle works

  1. n_crosses random crosses among the parents (the founders in cycle 1).

  2. Each F1 gives progeny_per_cross F2 plants, advanced by single-seed descent to Fline_generation lines, so a cycle makes n_crosses * progeny_per_cross lines.

  3. PYT: every line at pyt_locations x pyt_reps plots. The top n_ayt lines by trial mean go on.

  4. AYT: ayt_locations x ayt_reps plots. The top n_release lines are released and the top n_parents become the next cycle's parents.

Trial means carry error variance gxe_var / locations + plot_var / (locations * reps), where plot_var comes from the founders' plot_h2 and gxe_var is in units of the founder genetic variance, so extra locations average out genotype-by-environment noise that extra reps cannot.

Time and cost

A cycle takes line_generation / generations_per_year years in the nursery (crossing and selfing) plus one year for each trial. Cycles do not overlap, which keeps the model simple but understates the gain per year of programs that start new crosses every year. Cost adds crosses (cross_cost), single-seed-descent plants per generation (ssd_cost), trial plots (plot_cost, or pyt_plot_cost for the PYT when it is phenotyped differently) and, for nursery generations grown outside the main season (line_generation - ceiling(line_generation / generations_per_year) of them), offseason_cost per line per generation. Designs whose plots or cost per cycle exceed max_plots or max_cost are skipped as infeasible.

A different PYT phenotype

pyt_error multiplies the PYT error variance and pyt_plot_cost sets its cost per plot, so a cheaper but noisier screen, such as drone imagery or a visual score, can be compared with conventional yield plots.

Outcomes

release_gain (genetic value of the last cycle's releases, in founder genetic SDs), gain_per_year, gain_per_cost (per 1000 currency units), genetic_variance and expected_heterozygosity of the final parents (relative to the founders), accuracy and ayt_accuracy (correlation of PYT and AYT means with genetic value, among the lines in each trial), lines, plots and cost_per_cycle per cycle, total cost, years, and a yearly trajectory (see collect_trajectories()).

Examples

line_pipeline(n_ayt = tune(), ayt_locations = tune())
#> line_pipeline simulation spec (engine: AlphaSimR)
#> 
#> Tuned arguments:
#>   n_ayt = tune()
#>   ayt_locations = tune()
#> 
#> Fixed arguments:
#>   n_parents = 30
#>   n_crosses = 50
#>   progeny_per_cross = 20
#>   line_generation = 5
#>   generations_per_year = 2
#>   pyt_locations = 1
#>   pyt_reps = 1
#>   ayt_reps = 2
#>   n_release = 5
#>   cycles = 4
#>   gxe_var = 0.5
#>   cross_cost = 25
#>   ssd_cost = 2
#>   plot_cost = 15
#>   pyt_plot_cost = NA
#>   pyt_error = 1
#>   offseason_cost = 0
#>   max_plots = Inf
#>   max_cost = Inf
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
spec <- line_pipeline(n_ayt = tune(), ayt_locations = tune(), cycles = 3)
res <- tune_grid(spec, sim_replicates(10), grid = 9)
show_best(res, metric = "gain_per_year")
} # }
